long_biography.plain_text:
After studying economics at Leeds and business at Columbia, Irvine Laidlaw entered publishing and founded the Institute for International Research in 1973. He expanded IIR from specialist newsletters into conferences, exhibitions and corporate training. By 2005 it operated internationally at substantial scale; Informa bought the company, establishing the central liquidity event behind Laidlaw's fortune.

His role changed from operating an events company to directing private capital. He chairs Highland Group Holdings, a private investment group with documented projects in offshore wind, power generation and fibre infrastructure. He also founded Laidlaw Scholars Ventures, a venture fund backing companies created by alumni of the Laidlaw scholarship network. The latter is mission-linked investing, while Highland is the broader private investment platform.

uncertainties.detail: The record clearly establishes that Laidlaw founded and built IIR rather than inheriting that company. Reliable public evidence does not establish the source of his initial acquisition capital well enough to distinguish an independent from an advantaged start, so the broader Self-made classification is used.

Highland Group Holdings is currently identified as Lord Laidlaw's private investment group. Public transaction detail is selective, so the dossier describes documented energy, infrastructure and venture activity without implying a complete portfolio inventory.

Highland is the private investment platform. Laidlaw Scholars Ventures is a distinct mission-linked fund whose profits return to foundation programmes, and the Laidlaw Foundation itself is philanthropic rather than a personal wealth-producing asset.

The formal dignity is Baron Laidlaw of Rothiemay; current organisational materials use Lord Laidlaw. The proposal stores Lord in the separate title field and Irvine Laidlaw as the personal display name, avoiding the nonstandard form Baron Irvine Laidlaw.

A name-matched website presents inconsistent birth and education information and was rejected as an identity-verified personal site. No sufficiently verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X or TikTok profile was found; the existing exact Wikipedia URL is retained without modification.
Exact-name searches found no dedicated Irvine Laidlaw Forbes person profile.

Politics, donations to political organisations, peerage controversy, parliamentary matters, private-life material, allegations, legal matters, wealth estimates and yacht-specific research were excluded and played no role in the classifications or biographies.

review.notes:
Identity and the Media & Entertainment / Finance & Investments / Self-made / Family office principal classifications clear the 85-point gate. Review should preserve the distinction between IIR as the original wealth engine, Highland Group Holdings as the post-sale private investment platform and Laidlaw Scholars Ventures as a separate mission-linked fund. The title proposal replaces the nonstandard Baron prefix with customary Lord in the structured title field. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.
